statement: Every producer whose answer a consumer probes for a promise shape (typeof x.then, typeof x.catch, optional-chained or truthiness forms, instanceof Promise) answers one shape on every path: an I/O producer (transport sends, service command routing) returns a promise unconditionally, a synchronous-when-possible turn (the raft runtime's internal turn and the operation port's protocol answers, the serialized replica-mutation lane) returns a named settled-or-pending answer produced once at the producer so that no timing changes, and a service's apply mode is declared and validated once at registration instead of sniffed per entry; the consumer-side probes are deleted, and the pattern becomes an ESLint no-restricted-syntax selector so a value-or-promise return cannot reappear.

constraints.statement: A producer that answered synchronously on some path and now answers asynchronously names in the attempt every consumer whose ordering assumption changed and the witness that covers it.
The selector lands with the last deletion, never earlier.
The src/ changes land only behind an approving verification newer than the last attempt.
A probe is deleted only when its producer's answer has one shape (a promise, or a named settled-or-pending answer). Wrapping the consumer side in Promise.resolve keeps the ambiguity and is not a fix.

The raft runtime's internal turn stays synchronous when it can complete synchronously; a consumer that read a synchronous result keeps reading it on the settled branch. Making an internal turn always asynchronous is a raft semantics change outside this quest; a site where the named answer cannot hold without one is reported, not changed.
